0.long_answer: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) are a class of drugs generally prescribed as antidepressants to treat major depressive disorder. They work by inhibiting the reabsorption of serotonin in the brain, thereby increasing its availability, which helps improve mood and reduce anxiety. SSRIs are also effective in reducing symptoms of hypochondriasis, a condition characterized by an excessive preoccupation with having a serious illness. Their ability to alleviate both mood-related symptoms and somatic concerns makes them a useful option for patients suffering from hypochondriasis.
